title: Stir-Fried Water Spinach
subtitle: morning glory with garlic and fermented tofu
excerpt: Tender water spinach tossed at high heat with garlic and creamy fermented tofu in a classic Cantonese technique. Ready in 15 minutes and served alongside rice. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Stir-fried water spinach with fermented tofu (fu yu kong xin cai) is a staple of Cantonese home cooking and appears across Guangdong restaurants throughout South-East Asia and Hong Kong. The pairing of water spinach with fermented white tofu is documented in Cantonese cookbooks from the mid-twentieth century. The technique of blooming garlic in very hot oil before adding the greens is central to achieving wok hei at home.

glossaryTerms.definition: A semi-aquatic leafy vegetable with hollow stems and arrow-shaped leaves. Also called morning glory, kangkong or ong choy. It wilts quickly in a hot wok and has a mild, slightly sweet flavour. Sold in large bunches at Asian grocers.

Soft tofu cured in brine with salt, rice wine and spices. It comes in white (fu yu) and red (nan ru) varieties. White fermented tofu has a creamy, salty, mildly funky flavour and is used as a seasoning in Cantonese cooking.

Literally 'breath of the wok'. The slightly smoky, charred aroma that develops when food is cooked over very high heat in a well-seasoned wok. Achieved at home by getting the wok as hot as possible before adding oil.

content.text: This Cantonese dish takes about 15 minutes and serves 4 as a side.

Get the wok visibly smoking before you add the oil. This is the single most important step. If the wok is not hot enough, the water spinach steams rather than fries and turns limp and watery.

items.prepNote: tough stems removed, cut into 8 cm lengths

content.text: Wash the water spinach and shake dry. Remove any very thick or tough stems. Cut into 8 cm lengths.
Heat the wok over the highest heat available until it is visibly smoking, about 2 minutes.
Add the vegetable oil and swirl to coat the wok. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 20 seconds until fragrant and lightly golden at the edges.
Add the mashed fermented tofu and stir to combine with the garlic.
Tip in the water spinach all at once. Toss constantly with a spatula or tongs for 2 minutes until wilted but still bright green.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss for 30 more seconds.
Transfer to a plate immediately and serve with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Water spinach is watery and limp
items.cause: The wok was not hot enough.
items.fix: Heat the wok until smoking before adding oil. Cook in one batch, not two.

items.cause: Heat was too high when the garlic was added, or it cooked too long before the spinach went in.
items.fix: Add the garlic for no more than 20 seconds before adding the greens. Move quickly.

items.symptom: Fermented tofu makes the dish too salty
items.cause: Brands vary considerably in salt content.
items.fix: Use 1 cube instead of 2 and taste before adding any soy sauce.

content.text: Stir-fried water spinach is found across southern China and Southeast Asia. It is fast to cook and appears at hawker stalls and family tables. The hollow stems stay crunchy; the leaves wilt quickly. Do not cover the wok or the colour dulls. Serve immediately.
